messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: Error in Distance 'survey tab'
parts:
Nicholas

Sounds like your study area shape file is behaving as expected.  I'm not sure I'm with you regarding an "attributes table"; does this mean details of a shapefile containing your tracks?  If that is what you mean, then NO, the survey engine is not using that information.

Through specification of a survey design, you specify total effort and whether transects are parallel, zigzag, etc.  The design engine then produces repeated surveys consistent with those design characteristics.  The properties derived from those repeated simulated surveys are then reported.

Example 3 "creating a survey design" in Chapter 3 "Getting Started" of the users guide steps you through these procedures.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: Error in Distance 'survey tab'
parts:
Thanks for the project Nicholas.  I've made only a small amount of progress, but I'm starting to get a hint of what you are attempting. 

I learned your study area is ~340ha in size; a study area such as this would better be represented in units of UTMs; curvature of the earth is not going to matter for a study area of this size.

I am by no means clever about GIS systems, but one of the problems stems from latitude/longitude as the shapefile is organised, and metres for the projection.  Sometimes that works out, but more often than not is causes difficulties, and this is one of those cases.  When I produce a survey from my design criteria, the transect endpoint coordinates are produced in degrees

but the accompanying map uses UTM coordinates

rendering the resulting design invisible.


Moving on to the computed coverage probabilities; I saw your coverage grid also in units of degrees, spaced such that there are only 11 in the study area--that's really too few to get a good grasp of coverage.  On the other hand, from what I can tell looking at your map, these coverage grid points are ~350m apart.  If your sampler width is 282m, then placing a transect equidistant between any two coverage grid points will result in animals standing at either grid point to be "covered" detected.  Hence, for almost any design you place into that study area with a modest amount of effort, coverage probability will be uniformly high, if that is the true sampler width.  Consequently, your coverage map returns with all grid points covered all the time.  That's the explanation for the "binary" coverage probability you were experiencing.

I was able to achieve non-binary coverage probabilities by reducing survey effort (systematic parallel lines) to something on the order of 10km


My overall comments are:

- to use the design engine, you need not bring in the sightings and the tracks into Distance; they play no role in producing a survey design

- perform all your  cartographic transformations outside of Distance and use metres rather than degrees when in Distance

- your study area measures roughly 2.5km(NS) x 3.5km(EW), laying in ~20 transects systematically throughout the study area (sampling off trails) should be doable.

messages.subject: Re: Error in Distance 'survey tab'
parts:
Dear Eric,

Really can't thank you enough for having a look at my project. It seems I am way of the mark (embarrassingly so) with my entire project and use of distance. This survey was already completed in 340ha of forest with 1797km of survey effort that followed a trail system. 73 Observations were made with a distance and bearing measurement as well as cluster size and GPS point. The 282m width of the survey lines I used was taken from the maximum observed distance from the subject animals, which is possible since the area is made of steep limestone cliffs where observations can be made from across a valley.

I had imported the observations and survey trails from a GIS with the hope that I could:

A) analyse the coverage probability from the transect lines within the study area 
B) Estimate the population density of the target species with respects to the coverage bias observed by using trails as transects rather that having straight, evenly distributed transect lines

is any of this possible with distance software?

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: Error in Distance 'survey tab'
parts:
Nicholas

Afraid the answer is no on both counts.  Your transects were placed without any random component; there was no chance you were going to step off the trail system.  So probability of covering portion of study area along the tracks was 1.0, covering portions outside the trail system was 0.  You can make inference where you did go, but not where you had no chance of going.
